name: Barbell Bench Press
description: A foundational horizontal pressing movement for chest strength and mass.
instructions: Lie on the bench with feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack and lower the bar with control toward mid-chest.
Press the bar upward until arms are extended without locking out harshly.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
description: Targets the upper chest with an inclined pressing angle.
instructions: Set the bench to a moderate incline.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lower the bar to the upper chest.
Press upward while keeping shoulder blades set.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: A dumbbell variation that allows a greater range of motion.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells at chest level.
Press the dumbbells upward until arms are extended.
Lower with control to the sides of the chest.
commonMistakes: Going too deep and stressing shoulders

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: Upper-chest focused pressing with independent arm paths.
instructions: Set an incline bench and hold dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press upward over the upper chest.
Lower under control to the start position.
commonMistakes: Excessive incline turning it into a shoulder press

name: Machine Chest Press
description: A guided pressing machine useful for beginners and denser volume work.
instructions: Adjust the seat so handles align with mid-chest.
Grip the handles and press forward until arms nearly extend.
Return with control without slamming the stack.
commonMistakes: Seat height too high or too low

name: Cable Chest Fly
description: An isolation fly pattern emphasizing chest stretch and squeeze.
instructions: Set pulleys at chest height and step forward into a split stance.
With a soft elbow bend, bring the handles together in front of the chest.
Open the arms slowly against the cable resistance.
commonMistakes: Using momentum to swing the handles

name: Dumbbell Fly
description: A classic fly for chest isolation on a flat bench.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells above the chest, palms facing each other.
Open the arms in a wide arc with soft elbows.
Bring the dumbbells back together over the chest.
commonMistakes: Going too deep and stressing the shoulders
Bending and pressing instead of flying

name: Push Up
description: A foundational bodyweight horizontal press.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Lower the chest toward the floor while keeping a straight body line.
Press back to the start without sagging the hips.

name: Decline Push Up
description: A more challenging push-up variation emphasizing upper chest and shoulders.
instructions: Place feet elevated on a bench in a plank position.
Lower the chest toward the floor with control.
Press back up while keeping the core braced.

name: Pec Deck Fly
description: Machine fly pattern for controlled chest isolation.
instructions: Adjust the seat so handles align with chest height.
Bring the pads together in a controlled arc.
Return slowly to a comfortable stretch.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: A vertical pulling pattern targeting the lats.
instructions: Sit with thighs secured under the pads and grip the bar wide.
Pull the bar toward the upper chest while driving elbows down.
Control the return to a full stretch without losing torso position.

name: Pull Up
description: A demanding bodyweight vertical pull for back strength.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull the chest toward the bar by driving elbows down.
Lower with control to a full hang.
commonMistakes: Kipping when strict reps are intended

name: Assisted Pull Up
description: A regression that builds pull-up strength with support.
instructions: Select an assistance level that allows controlled reps.
Pull the chest toward the handles or bar.
Lower slowly without dropping into the stretch.
commonMistakes: Using too little assistance and losing form

name: Barbell Row
description: A bent-over horizontal row for overall back thickness.
instructions: Hinge at the hips with a soft knee bend and grip the bar.
Pull the bar toward the lower torso.
Lower under control while keeping a neutral spine.

name: Dumbbell Row
description: A unilateral row that reduces lower-back demand.
instructions: Place one hand and knee on a bench, holding a dumbbell in the free hand.
Pull the dumbbell toward the hip while keeping the torso stable.
Lower with control.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: A seated horizontal pull with constant cable tension.
instructions: Sit tall with feet on the platform and a slight knee bend.
Pull the handle to the torso while squeezing the shoulder blades.
Extend the arms under control without rounding forward.

name: Chest Supported Row
description: A row variation that limits cheating via torso momentum.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench or use a chest-supported machine.
Pull the weights toward the hips.
Lower slowly while keeping the chest glued to the pad.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad

name: Straight Arm Pulldown
description: An isolation pattern emphasizing lat engagement with long levers.
instructions: Stand facing a high cable with a straight-arm grip.
Keep arms nearly straight and pull the bar toward the thighs.
Control the return to overhead without arching excessively.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows into a press-down
Using the lower back to yank

name: Face Pull
description: A rear-delt and upper-back health movement.
instructions: Set a cable or band at upper-chest height with a rope attachment.
Pull toward the face while externally rotating the shoulders.
Squeeze the rear delts and return with control.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a heavy row

name: Inverted Row
description: A scalable horizontal pull using bodyweight.
instructions: Set a bar at about waist height and hang underneath with a straight body.
Pull the chest to the bar.
Lower under control without sagging the hips.

name: Chin Up
description: A supinated vertical pull with greater biceps involvement.
instructions: Hang with an underhand grip about shoulder width.
Pull the chest toward the bar.
Lower with control to a full hang.
commonMistakes: Kipping when strict reps are intended

name: Barbell Overhead Press
description: A standing vertical press for shoulder and upper-body strength.
instructions: Stand with the bar at shoulder height and brace the core.
Press the bar overhead until arms are extended.
Lower to the shoulders with control.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A versatile overhead press using dumbbells.
instructions: Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press overhead until arms are extended.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Arnold Press
description: A rotating dumbbell press that challenges the delts through a long path.
instructions: Start with palms facing you at shoulder height.
Rotate the palms forward while pressing overhead.
Reverse the motion on the way down.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: An isolation raise for the lateral deltoids.
instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells at the sides.
Raise the arms out to the sides until near shoulder height.
Lower under control without swinging.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: Constant-tension lateral raise using a cable.
instructions: Stand beside a low cable holding the handle in the far hand.
Raise the arm laterally to about shoulder height.
Lower slowly against the cable.

name: Rear Delt Fly
description: Targets the posterior deltoids.
instructions: Hinge forward or use a rear-delt machine.
Open the arms out to the sides with soft elbows.
Squeeze the rear delts, then return with control.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a heavy back row

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
description: Isolation for the anterior deltoids.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of the thighs.
Raise one or both arms to shoulder height.
Lower under control.

name: Upright Row
description: A vertical pull emphasizing delts and upper traps—use a comfortable range.
instructions: Hold the implement in front of the thighs.
Pull upward leading with the elbows to about chest height.
Lower with control.
commonMistakes: Pulling too high and stressing wrists or shoulders

name: Barbell Curl
description: A classic bilateral biceps curl.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
Curl the bar toward the shoulders without swinging.
Lower under control to full extension.

name: Dumbbell Curl
description: A standard dumbbell biceps curl.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at the sides.
Curl the weights up while keeping elbows close to the torso.
Lower slowly.

name: Hammer Curl
description: Neutral-grip curl emphasizing brachialis and forearms.
instructions: Hold dumbbells with a neutral grip.
Curl the weights toward the shoulders.
Lower under control.
commonMistakes: Rotating into a supinated curl unintentionally

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
description: Places the biceps in a lengthened starting position.
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with arms hanging behind the torso.
Curl the dumbbells without swinging.
Lower fully to stretch the biceps.

name: Cable Curl
description: Cable curl with continuous tension.
instructions: Stand facing a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl toward the shoulders while keeping elbows still.
Control the eccentric.

name: Preacher Curl
description: A supported curl that reduces cheating.
instructions: Position upper arms on the preacher pad.
Curl the weight toward the shoulders.
Lower until arms are nearly extended without hyperextending.
commonMistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad

name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
description: A staple triceps isolation movement.
instructions: Stand at a high cable with elbows pinned to the sides.
Extend the arms downward until nearly straight.
Return until forearms are about parallel without moving the elbows.
commonMistakes: Using the shoulders to push down

name: Overhead Cable Extension
description: Emphasizes the long head of the triceps in a stretched position.
instructions: Face away from a cable set high or use a rope overhead.
Extend the elbows until arms are straight.
Control the return into a stretch.

name: Skull Crusher
description: A lying triceps extension pattern.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding the weight above the chest.
Bend the elbows to lower toward the forehead or behind the head.
Extend the elbows to return.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension
description: A simple overhead triceps stretch-and-extend movement.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell overhead with elbows pointing up.
Lower behind the head by bending the elbows.
Extend back to the start.

name: Close Grip Bench Press
description: A compound press that shifts emphasis toward the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a bench with a narrower-than-normal grip.
Lower the bar to the lower chest with elbows closer to the torso.
Press back up with control.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows like a wide press

name: Diamond Push Up
description: A close-hand push-up variation for triceps emphasis.
instructions: Form a diamond hand position under the chest in a plank.
Lower the chest toward the hands.
Press back up while keeping the core tight.

name: Triceps Dip
description: A compound push emphasizing the triceps.
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars or a sturdy bench.
Lower by bending the elbows to a comfortable depth.
Press back to extension.
commonMistakes: Going too deep and stressing shoulders

name: Wrist Curl
description: Targets the wrist flexors.
instructions: Sit with forearms on thighs and wrists hanging off the knees.
Curl the weight upward using the wrists.
Lower under control.
commonMistakes: Using the arms instead of wrists

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
description: Targets the wrist extensors.
instructions: Sit with forearms supported and palms facing down.
Extend the wrists upward.
Lower slowly.

name: Farmer Carry
description: A loaded carry that builds grip, core, and posture.
instructions: Pick up heavy implements at the sides and stand tall.
Walk with controlled steps while bracing the core.
Set the weights down with control.

name: Barbell Squat
description: A foundational bilateral lower-body strength movement.
instructions: Set the bar on the upper back and brace the core.
Break at the hips and knees to descend to a comfortable depth.
Drive through mid-foot to stand tall.

name: Front Squat
description: A squat variation with greater quadriceps and upright torso demand.
instructions: Rack the bar on the front delts with elbows high.
Descend while keeping the torso more upright.
Stand by driving through the mid-foot.

name: Goblet Squat
description: A beginner-friendly squat teaching pattern.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest.
Squat down between the knees while keeping the chest up.
Stand tall without rounding forward.

name: Leg Press
description: A machine compound for lower-body loading with back support.
instructions: Sit with feet mid-platform about shoulder width.
Lower the sled by bending the knees under control.
Press back without locking out harshly.
commonMistakes: Lowering too deep and rounding the low back

name: Leg Extension
description: Isolation for the quadriceps.
instructions: Adjust the pad on the lower shins and sit tall.
Extend the knees until nearly straight.
Lower under control.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: A hip-hinge pattern emphasizing the posterior chain.
instructions: Stand tall holding the weight at the thighs.
Hinge at the hips while keeping a soft knee bend and neutral spine.
Drive the hips forward to stand.

name: Leg Curl
description: Isolation for the hamstrings.
instructions: Position the pad on the lower calves and lie or sit per machine design.
Curl the heels toward the glutes.
Lower slowly.
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A unilateral squat pattern for legs and balance.
instructions: Place the rear foot on a bench and the front foot forward.
Lower until the front thigh is near parallel.
Drive through the front foot to stand.
commonMistakes: Front foot too close causing knee discomfort

name: Walking Lunge
description: A dynamic unilateral lower-body movement.
instructions: Step forward into a lunge with both knees bending.
Push through the front foot to bring the rear leg through into the next step.
Keep the torso upright.
commonMistakes: Short choppy steps with no control

name: Hip Thrust
description: A primary glute-strengthening hip extension pattern.
instructions: Set upper back on a bench with knees bent and feet planted.
Drive through the heels to raise the hips until the torso is near parallel.
Lower under control.
commonMistakes: Overextending the lower back at the top
Feet too far forward or back

name: Glute Bridge
description: A simple floor glute activation and strength drill.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Press through the heels to lift the hips.
Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back instead of using glutes

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: Targets the gastrocnemius with a standing pattern.
instructions: Stand with the balls of the feet on a step or platform.
Rise onto the toes.
Lower into a comfortable stretch.

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: Emphasizes the soleus in a bent-knee position.
instructions: Sit with the pads on the thighs and feet on the platform.
Raise the heels as high as comfortable.
Lower into a stretch.

name: Hack Squat
description: A machine squat pattern with guided torso support.
instructions: Position shoulders under the pads and feet mid-platform.
Descend by bending the knees while keeping the back against the pad.
Drive up without locking harshly.
commonMistakes: Feet too low causing excessive knee stress
Losing back contact with the pad

name: Step Up
description: A unilateral stepping pattern for legs and stability.
instructions: Place one foot fully on a box or bench.
Drive through the lead foot to stand tall on the box.
Step down with control and repeat.
commonMistakes: Pushing off the trailing leg excessively
Using a box that is too high

name: Sumo Deadlift
description: A wide-stance hinge emphasizing glutes and adductors.
instructions: Take a wide stance with toes angled out and grip the bar inside the legs.
Brace and drive through the floor to stand.
Hinge back to lower with a neutral spine.

name: Conventional Deadlift
description: A fundamental full-body strength pull from the floor.
instructions: Stand with mid-foot under the bar and grip outside the legs.
Brace, push the floor away, and stand tall.
Hinge to return the bar with control.
commonMistakes: Jerking the bar off the floor

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
description: A dumbbell hinge progression for the posterior chain.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at the sides or in front of the thighs.
Hinge at the hips with a soft knee bend.
Drive the hips forward to stand.
commonMistakes: Letting the weights drift too far forward

name: Smith Machine Squat
description: A guided squat using the Smith machine path.
instructions: Position the bar on the upper back within the Smith guides.
Unlock and descend to a comfortable depth.
Drive up and re-rack securely.
commonMistakes: Feet placed uncomfortably far forward or back

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
description: A guided horizontal press on the Smith machine.
instructions: Set a bench under the Smith bar and unrack carefully.
Lower the bar to mid-chest.
Press up and re-rack.

name: Cable Kickback
description: An isolation hip-extension pattern for the glutes.
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable and face the stack.
Extend the working leg back while keeping the hips square.
Return without twisting.

name: Plank
description: An isometric anti-extension core drill.
instructions: Set up on forearms and toes with a straight body line.
Brace the core and squeeze the glutes.
Hold while breathing steadily.

name: Side Plank
description: An anti-lateral-flexion core hold.
instructions: Lie on one side and prop up on the forearm.
Lift the hips to form a straight line.
Hold without rotating forward or back.

name: Cable Crunch
description: A loaded flexion pattern for the abdominals.
instructions: Kneel facing a high cable with a rope at the shoulders.
Crunch the ribcage toward the pelvis.
Return under control without yanking the stack.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: A hanging core flexion progression.
instructions: Hang from a bar with stable shoulders.
Raise the knees toward the chest.
Lower without swinging.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: A more advanced hanging flexion variation.
instructions: Hang from a bar with legs straight.
Raise the legs toward horizontal or higher while controlling the torso.
Lower slowly without kipping.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: A demanding anti-extension rolling pattern.
instructions: Kneel holding an ab wheel under the shoulders.
Roll forward while keeping the ribs down and hips extended.
Pull back to the start without sagging.
commonMistakes: Going out too far too soon

name: Dead Bug
description: A controlled anti-extension drill for core stability.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent at 90 degrees.
Extend opposite arm and leg while keeping the low back pressed down.
Return and switch sides.

name: Bird Dog
description: A stability pattern for core and posterior chain coordination.
instructions: Start on hands and knees.
Extend opposite arm and leg while keeping the hips level.
Return and switch sides.

name: Russian Twist
description: A rotational core conditioning movement.
instructions: Sit with a slight backward lean and feet elevated or planted.
Rotate the torso side to side with control.
Keep the chest tall.
commonMistakes: Using only the arms to swing a load

name: Cable Woodchop
description: A rotational core pattern using a cable path.
instructions: Set a cable high or low depending on chop direction.
Rotate the torso while keeping hips relatively stable.
Return under control and switch sides as programmed.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: A ballistic hip-hinge conditioning pattern.
instructions: Hinge and hike the kettlebell back between the legs.
Snap the hips forward to swing the bell to about chest height.
Let the bell pendulum back into the next hinge.

name: Burpee
description: A full-body conditioning drill combining squat, plank, and stand.
instructions: From standing, drop into a squat and place hands on the floor.
Kick or step to a plank, optionally add a push-up.
Jump the feet forward and extend to stand or jump.

name: Mountain Climber
description: An alternating knee-drive conditioning pattern from a plank.
instructions: Start in a high plank.
Drive one knee toward the chest, then quickly switch legs.
Keep the hips level and shoulders stacked.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the hips up and down

name: Medicine Ball Slam
description: A power and conditioning slam using a medicine ball.
instructions: Lift the ball overhead while rising onto the toes slightly.
Slam the ball into the floor by hinging and engaging the core.
Pick the ball up and repeat.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back on the pickup
Using a ball that is too heavy to control

name: Jump Rope
description: A classic low-equipment cardio conditioning drill.
instructions: Hold the rope handles with elbows close to the body.
Jump lightly on the balls of the feet as the rope passes under.
Keep jumps small and rhythmical.

name: Box Jump
description: A lower-body power drill emphasizing soft landings.
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box with feet shoulder width.
Load the hips and jump onto the box softly.
Stand tall, then step down carefully.
commonMistakes: Jumping down repeatedly instead of stepping down

name: Battle Rope Wave
description: An upper-body conditioning pattern using battle ropes.
instructions: Hold the rope ends in an athletic stance.
Create alternating or simultaneous waves with the arms.
Keep the core braced and knees soft.
commonMistakes: Standing fully upright and losing power

name: Cat Cow
description: A gentle spinal mobility drill.
instructions: Start on hands and knees.
Alternate arching and rounding the spine slowly with the breath.
Move through a comfortable range only.

name: World Greatest Stretch
description: A flowing multi-planar mobility sequence often used in warm-ups.
instructions: Step into a lunge and place the same-side hand inside the front foot.
Rotate the chest upward reaching the arm to the ceiling.
Return and switch sides.

name: Hamstring Stretch
description: A simple static or gentle dynamic hamstring stretch.
instructions: Sit or stand and hinge gently to lengthen the back of the thigh.
Hold a mild stretch without bouncing.
Breathe and ease out of the position.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
description: A common stretch for the chest and anterior shoulder.
instructions: Place the forearm on a doorway with the elbow near shoulder height.
Step through gently until a stretch is felt across the chest.
Hold, then switch sides.
commonMistakes: Elevating the shoulder toward the ear

name: Band Pull Apart
description: A warm-up activation drill for the upper back and rear delts.
instructions: Hold a light band at shoulder height with arms extended.
Pull the band apart by squeezing the shoulder blades.
Return with control.

name: Glute Bridge March
description: A glute activation progression from a static bridge.
instructions: Hold a glute bridge position.
Slowly lift one foot a few inches, then switch.
Keep the hips level throughout.
